rappel_detail.anchor: fixed slings and rap rings, or a nut anchor built on the spot
rappel_detail.station: Summit area, at the top of the West Ridge crest. The fixed stations here have been found both freshly rebuilt and badly tattered, so inspect each one.
rappel_detail.notes: West Ridge rappel 1 of 5 on a single 60-70 m rope.
hazards: Back up or replace any tattered tat: carry extra cord and a knife.

rappel_detail.anchor: fixed slings and rap rings of varying quality, or natural nut and cam anchors
rappel_detail.station: Next station down the upper West Ridge crest. Some stations sit off to the side rather than straight below the last, to keep you out of the fall line.
rappel_detail.notes: West Ridge rappel 2 of 5 on a single 60-70 m rope.
hazards: Some rappels traverse sideways to reach the next anchor. Loose, rockfall-prone rock sits on these traversing lines, so move one at a time and keep the rope out of the fall line.

rappel_detail.notes: West Ridge rappel 5 of 5 on a single 60-70 m rope. Below it, coil the rope and downclimb 3rd-4th class terrain to the notch at the top of the South Face.

rappel_detail.anchor: fixed slings and rap rings, or natural anchors
rappel_detail.station: The notch at the top of the South Face, reached by the downclimb from the last ridge station.

rappel_detail.anchor: fixed slings and rap rings, or natural anchors
rappel_detail.station: Next station down the South Face. Stations here often lie well to one side of the last one, not straight down, so look left and right before committing.
hazards: Several South Face rappels need a hard traverse one way or the other to reach the next anchor. Weight the rope before you swing, and watch for rock knocked loose by the rope.

rappel_detail.station: Lowest station on the South Face, above the Terror Glacier.
rappel_detail.notes: South Face rappel 9 of 9. This one often takes the full length of the doubled rope to reach flat glacier snow; knot the ends. Rope up for glacier travel as soon as you are down.
hazards: Crevasses on the Terror Glacier start right at the bottom of the rappel.

set.rappels: There is no East Ridge descent. 14 single-rope rappels with a 60-70 m rope: 5 down the upper West Ridge, a scramble down to a notch, then 9 down the South Face to the Terror Glacier. With two ropes, parties have instead made seven double-rope rappels straight down the West Ridge.
set.rappel_count_note: The descent is the same as the West Ridge and South Face routes’. Counted for one 60-70 m rope, which is what most parties now carry: 5 rappels on the upper West Ridge and 9 on the South Face below the notch. The stations are spaced for a single rope. With two ropes, parties have descended the whole West Ridge in seven double-rope rappels off natural anchors instead, skipping the South Face. Anchors on the ridge were reported rebuilt in June 2024, but stations vary and some are tattered, so carry cord to back them up. Two landmarks on the ridge part of the line: a large horn anchor, and a fixed three-pin anchor where the rappel goes down and climber’s right off a large overhang and hangs free, with the next station offset rather than straight below.
